description: Issue #839: when a program contains BOTH kinds of declaration-slot collision, the first one in SOURCE ORDER halts it. Here a duplicate `tally` on line 4 precedes a built-in `define forward` on line 7, and the duplicate is what is reported — the run stops there, so the later `ol-reserved-word` is never produced. This is the ordering property, deliberately separated from the *priority* property (`ol-reserved-word` beats `ol-duplicate-definition` when ONE name is both), which is a check-stage concern because `check()` reports every finding while `execute()` stops at the first. Reversing the two blocks would report `ol-reserved-word` at line 7 instead, so the fixture is sensitive to the order rather than to the mere presence of two collisions.

diagnostics.message: you already defined tally on line 1.
